From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Prepared by:** Buyer AI legal assistant
**Status:** Privileged / for internal negotiation use

## 0. Threshold point: do not accept the Seller's framing of the review

Before the substance, two features of the Seller's package need to be called out because they would, if accepted, shape everything else:

1. **"Settled at principal level… marked FINAL… not intended to be re-opened."** Our playbook is explicit that the 20%/AUD 4.8m cap and the 18‑month claims period are *conditional fallbacks* usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and that **no such authority has been given**. The Seller's assertion that these were agreed at principal level is unverified and inconsistent with our instructions. We should treat every position in the package as open and, separately, confirm with Amelia Frost that no side agreement has been reached outside the written record.

2. **"Reviewer efficiency note" / [STANDARD] labels.** The Seller has pre-labelled almost every contentious clause as cleared and asked us to review only [OPEN] items (there are none). This is the counterparty's categorisation, not ours. Nothing in a Seller draft can narrow the scope of our review. I have reviewed every provision.

The "market context" preamble (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) is advocacy, not evidence, and in several respects the draft falls below even the range the Seller itself describes (e.g. the basket is tipping, not first-dollar; fundamental warranties are collapsed into the general regime).

---

## 1. Clause-by-clause departures from the Buyer playbook

### 1.1 General warranty cap (cl 12.1) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position; 20% is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which does not exist.
- **Reasoning:** Accepting the Seller's number now would spend our fallback for nothing in return and would be outside our authority. The Seller's "FINAL" label does not change that.
- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 6,000,000. Hold 20% in reserve as a trade for concessions elsewhere (e.g. fundamental regime, Bluefen condition), and only with documented approval.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Reasoning:** Three separate departures. The de minimis is 5× ours, the basket 5× ours, and the shift from a tipping basket to a deductible basket permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of every valid claim. In a business with ~30% customer concentration and several unresolved DD items, mid-sized claims are the likely profile; the Seller's thresholds would screen most of them out.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. If any movement is given, protect the tipping mechanic above all.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims, plus a sweep that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given). Tax/IP/Title/payment/covenant categories must stay separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Reasoning:** 24 months captures at least one full post-completion audit cycle and the FY27 Bluefen renewal window. The "applies to all Claims" sweep is the more dangerous element: it would silently pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims into an 18‑month window.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the all‑Claims sweep; replace with a positive statement that general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and that each other category has its own regime.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** capacity and title subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime; 100% of price cap; at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** We are paying AUD 24m for 100% of the shares. If the Seller does not own them, or lacks capacity, our recovery under the Seller's draft would be capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred after 18 months. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept 20 cents in the dollar on the one thing the price is for.
- **Push back:** Non-negotiable. Separate schedule for Fundamental Warranties with 100% cap, six-year period, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** universal application.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, the Seller's limitations would purport to cap and time-bar even fraud. Beyond being unenforceable in part under NSW law, agreeing to it would signal we are prepared to trade on this point, which we are not.
- **Push back:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that prevails over cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. Also exclude specific indemnities and Fundamental Warranties from exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language.

### 1.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter §1) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD‑002 to DD‑012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure converts every document into a defence to every warranty, regardless of whether the relevant issue was fairly flagged. The public-records limb goes further, deeming us to know things not even in the data room. Combined with cl 8.3 (below) it would hollow out the warranties almost entirely.
- **Push back:** Delete §1.1 and §1.2 general disclosure. Require that only matters fairly disclosed, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, qualify the warranties. Note that the Seller's own §1.4 reservation ("nothing admits… that any consent, payment, notice… is legally required") shows the general disclosures are not intended to be fair, specific disclosures – they are a shield, not information.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any knowledge qualifier must be tied to **named Seller knowledge persons** with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard – it bars claims about things we did not actually know but theoretically could have found. Imputing advisers' knowledge compounds it. This clause inverts the warranty allocation: the Seller gives warranties, but the Buyer bears the risk of anything in the record.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. If any knowledge concept survives, it must be *Seller's* knowledge (named individuals, after due enquiry) qualifying specified warranties only.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – **MATERIAL / COMPLETION-CRITICAL**
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a material customer.
- **Disclosure Letter §2:** confirms ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%), that consent is conditional under cl 11.3, and that **no final consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction is in the data room**.
- **Reasoning:** A conditional consent that is "satisfied on delivery" could be delivered with unmet conditions and leave Bluefen free to terminate post-Completion. Thirty percent of revenue is the single largest value risk in the deal.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent (or conditional consent plus documentary evidence each cl 11.3 condition is met) delivered before Completion, in a form reasonably acceptable to the Buyer. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with a Buyer right to terminate if not satisfied by the Long Stop Date. Consider a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates within 12 months citing the change of control.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – **MATERIAL / COMPLETION-CRITICAL**
- **Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases **at** Completion; any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Disclosure Letter §3:** confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, change-of-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions, no repayment, no discharge.
- **Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If we complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding and only a promise of a later release, we (a) have paid for an unencumbered company and received an encumbered one, (b) are exposed to a change-of-control default under cl 8.1 from the moment we own the shares, and (c) depend on the Seller's post-completion cooperation.
- **Push back:** Payout letter dated no earlier than two business days before Completion; repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges delivered into escrow at Completion. No post-completion release without Amelia Frost's written approval and a bank undertaking addressed to the Buyer.

### 1.10 Employee bonuses – DD‑005 (funds flow) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised."
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or demonstrably seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Disclosure Letter §5:** confirms the bonuses are triggered by Completion and continued employment, are absent from the funds flow, and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Reasoning:** The bonuses are a company obligation that crystallises on our Completion. If not funded from the price, the Buyer pays them post-Completion, together with superannuation guarantee, payroll tax and leave accruals – realistically AUD 480,000–520,000 all-in. "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism.
- **Push back:** Either (i) a funds-flow line item deducting AUD 420,000 plus a Seller-warranted on-cost figure from the price, or (ii) a Seller covenant to pay the gross amount into the Company pre-Completion with evidence, backed by a specific indemnity. Require the Seller to confirm on-cost treatment in writing.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- **Playbook:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way.
- **Disclosure Letter §4:** cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD‑010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment.
- **Reasoning:** The risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables, and may not own them even after payment if no confirmatory assignment is obtained. An indemnity for the fee alone does not cover loss of IP, third-party claims, or the cost of re-development.
- **Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment (bank record, not DD‑010) and an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. (b) Broaden cl 11.1 to indemnify all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to Project Materials under DD‑004, uncapped by the general regime, with the SOW3 payment preserved as a cure mechanism rather than the ceiling.

### 1.12 Export/privacy incident – DD‑006 (cl 4.6 / Sch 6) – **OPEN / MONITOR**
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified exposure in either direction.
- **Disclosure Letter §6:** ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification question unresolved.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the disclosure itself does not support – the investigation is preliminary. We should not accept a materiality characterisation, nor assert a breach ourselves.
- **Push back:** Seller covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates pre-Completion; an express pre-Completion warranty bring-down on this item; a specific indemnity for any notification, regulatory or third-party cost arising from the DD‑006 event, outside the general cap. Remove "not expected to be material" from Sch 6.

### 1.13 Sandbar renewals (DD‑008 / DD‑011) – **ASSESS**
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Disclosure Letter §8:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course" but its own disclosure disclaims any view on that. We should not automatically treat this as Debt, but we need the facts.
- **Push back:** Request copies of the three agreements, renewal dates, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued at Completion. Commercial/finance to decide treatment after review.

### 1.14 Tax / IP warranties – **OPEN**
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; assume no resolution; keep separate from the general regime.
- **Reasoning:** This is a second attempt (with cl 13's "all Claims" sweep) to fold Tax and IP into the 20%/18‑month/tipping-basket regime by assertion. Nothing has been agreed.
- **Push back:** Mark Tax and IP as [OPEN] in our turn. Propose a separate Tax regime (seven-year period, claims from first dollar) and a separate IP regime at minimum. Do not propose unlimited liability.

### 1.15 Title evidence (DD‑012) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD‑012."
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD‑012 is a Seller-supplied internal document.
- **Disclosure Letter §10:** the Seller itself notes DD‑012 is "the source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Reasoning:** A company's own register is evidence of what the company recorded, not independent proof. It does not disclose encumbrances (PPSR), director/shareholder authority, or historic transfer defects.
- **Push back:** Independent ASIC extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, review of share transfer history and any shareholder/option/convertible instruments, and a Seller board minute and shareholder resolution approving the sale. Fundamental Warranties on title to remain uncapped per §1.4.

### 1.16 Office lease (DD‑007) and Mossvale (DD‑009) – **LOWER PRIORITY / CONFIRM**
- Disclosure Letter §7 and §9 characterise these as notification-only / not triggered by a share sale. These appear consistent with our understanding but we should read the clauses ourselves and require a Seller covenant to give any required notices pre-Completion. Not a negotiation point unless the documents say otherwise.

---

## 2. Pattern observed

Read together, the Seller's draft is constructed so that each of the following would operate cumulatively:

- whole-data-room and public-record deemed disclosure (§1.6), plus
- buyer constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers (§1.7), plus
- high tipping-to-deductible thresholds (§1.2), plus
- a reduced cap (§1.1) and reduced period (§1.3), plus
- collapse of Fundamental, Tax, IP and indemnity claims into that regime (§1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.14).

The practical result would be a warranty package under which very few claims could ever be brought, and none for the matters we are paying for. This is why the "FINAL / cleared" labelling matters: it is an attempt to lock in the architecture before the individual terms are negotiated.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Reject the framing**
1. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement exists on cap or period. Record in our cover note that all terms remain open and that we do not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation.

**Non-negotiable (deal architecture)**
2. Fundamental/Title Warranties: separate regime, 100% cap, six years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
3. Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct: express overriding carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
4. Delete the cl 13 "all Claims" sweep and the "Tax/IP settled under general regime" assertion; keep each category separate.
5. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar; delete §1.1/§1.2 general disclosure; specific fair disclosure only.

**Economic terms – revert to playbook**
6. Cap AUD 6,000,000 (25%). Hold 20% only as an authorised trade.
7. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery.
8. Claims period 24 months.

**Completion mechanics**
9. Bluefen: CP requiring effective consent and evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; Buyer termination right; consider specific indemnity.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases and PPSR discharges at Completion; no post-completion release without irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
11. DD‑005 bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or evidenced Seller pre-funding, with specific indemnity; Seller to confirm on-cost treatment.
12. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence; do not rely on DD‑012.

**Specific risk items**
13. Ironquay: pre-Completion proof of cleared payment and confirmatory assignment; broaden cl 11.1 to cover IP title defects, preserving the SOW3 cure.
14. DD‑006: preservation and investigation covenants, written updates, bring-down, specific indemnity; strike "not expected to be material."
15. Sandbar: request agreements and accrual position; decide treatment on the facts.
16. Lease/Mossvale: confirm clause wording; Seller covenant to give notices.

**Housekeeping**
17. Note the Seller's §1.4 reservation (no admission of anything) and §11 (Buyer must evaluate everything itself): these confirm the Disclosure Letter is defensive, not informative, and reinforce the need for specific disclosure and independent verification.

Happy to turn this into a mark-up of the SPA clauses or a response letter to Harbourglass's counsel on instruction.

- **Reasoning:** Three separate departures. The de minimis is 5× ours, the basket 5× ours, and the shift from a tipping basket to a deductible basket permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of every valid claim. In a business with ~30% customer concentration and several unresolved DD items, mid-sized claims are the likely profile; the Seller's thresholds would screen most of them out.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. If any movement is given, protect the tipping mechanic above all.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims, plus a sweep that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given). Tax/IP/Title/payment/covenant categories must stay separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Reasoning:** 24 months captures at least one full post-completion audit cycle and the FY27 Bluefen renewal window. The "applies to all Claims" sweep is the more dangerous element: it would silently pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims into an 18‑month window.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the all‑Claims sweep; replace with a positive statement that general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and that each other category has its own regime.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** capacity and title subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime; 100% of price cap; at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** We are paying AUD 24m for 100% of the shares. If the Seller does not own them, or lacks capacity, our recovery under the Seller's draft would be capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred after 18 months. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept 20 cents in the dollar on the one thing the price is for.
- **Push back:** Non-negotiable. Separate schedule for Fundamental Warranties with 100% cap, six-year period, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** universal application.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** As drafted, the Seller's limitations would purport to cap and time-bar even fraud. Beyond being unenforceable in part under NSW law, agreeing to it would signal we are prepared to trade on this point, which we are not.
- **Push back:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out that prevails over cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. Also exclude specific indemnities and Fundamental Warranties from exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language.

### 1.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter §1) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD‑002 to DD‑012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure converts every document into a defence to every warranty, regardless of whether the relevant issue was fairly flagged. The public-records limb goes further, deeming us to know things not even in the data room. Combined with cl 8.3 (below) it would hollow out the warranties almost entirely.
- **Push back:** Delete §1.1 and §1.2 general disclosure. Require that only matters fairly disclosed, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, qualify the warranties. Note that the Seller's own §1.4 reservation ("nothing admits… that any consent, payment, notice… is legally required") shows the general disclosures are not intended to be fair, specific disclosures – they are a shield, not information.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any knowledge qualifier must be tied to **named Seller knowledge persons** with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard – it bars claims about things we did not actually know but theoretically could have found. Imputing advisers' knowledge compounds it. This clause inverts the warranty allocation: the Seller gives warranties, but the Buyer bears the risk of anything in the record.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. If any knowledge concept survives, it must be *Seller's* knowledge (named individuals, after due enquiry) qualifying specified warranties only.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – **MATERIAL / COMPLETION-CRITICAL**
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a material customer.
- **Disclosure Letter §2:** confirms ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%), that consent is conditional under cl 11.3, and that **no final consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction is in the data room**.
- **Reasoning:** A conditional consent that is "satisfied on delivery" could be delivered with unmet conditions and leave Bluefen free to terminate post-Completion. Thirty percent of revenue is the single largest value risk in the deal.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent (or conditional consent plus documentary evidence each cl 11.3 condition is met) delivered before Completion, in a form reasonably acceptable to the Buyer. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with a Buyer right to terminate if not satisfied by the Long Stop Date. Consider a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates within 12 months citing the change of control.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – **MATERIAL / COMPLETION-CRITICAL**
- **Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases **at** Completion; any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Disclosure Letter §3:** confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, change-of-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions, no repayment, no discharge.
- **Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. If we complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding and only a promise of a later release, we (a) have paid for an unencumbered company and received an encumbered one, (b) are exposed to a change-of-control default under cl 8.1 from the moment we own the shares, and (c) depend on the Seller's post-completion cooperation.
- **Push back:** Payout letter dated no earlier than two business days before Completion; repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges delivered into escrow at Completion. No post-completion release without Amelia Frost's written approval and a bank undertaking addressed to the Buyer.

### 1.10 Employee bonuses – DD‑005 (funds flow) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised."
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or demonstrably seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Disclosure Letter §5:** confirms the bonuses are triggered by Completion and continued employment, are absent from the funds flow, and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Reasoning:** The bonuses are a company obligation that crystallises on our Completion. If not funded from the price, the Buyer pays them post-Completion, together with superannuation guarantee, payroll tax and leave accruals – realistically AUD 480,000–520,000 all-in. "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism.
- **Push back:** Either (i) a funds-flow line item deducting AUD 420,000 plus a Seller-warranted on-cost figure from the price, or (ii) a Seller covenant to pay the gross amount into the Company pre-Completion with evidence, backed by a specific indemnity. Require the Seller to confirm on-cost treatment in writing.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- **Playbook:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way.
- **Disclosure Letter §4:** cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD‑010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment.
- **Reasoning:** The risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables, and may not own them even after payment if no confirmatory assignment is obtained. An indemnity for the fee alone does not cover loss of IP, third-party claims, or the cost of re-development.
- **Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment (bank record, not DD‑010) and an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. (b) Broaden cl 11.1 to indemnify all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to Project Materials under DD‑004, uncapped by the general regime, with the SOW3 payment preserved as a cure mechanism rather than the ceiling.

### 1.12 Export/privacy incident – DD‑006 (cl 4.6 / Sch 6) – **OPEN / MONITOR**
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified exposure in either direction.
- **Disclosure Letter §6:** ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification question unresolved.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the disclosure itself does not support – the investigation is preliminary. We should not accept a materiality characterisation, nor assert a breach ourselves.
- **Push back:** Seller covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates pre-Completion; an express pre-Completion warranty bring-down on this item; a specific indemnity for any notification, regulatory or third-party cost arising from the DD‑006 event, outside the general cap. Remove "not expected to be material" from Sch 6.

### 1.13 Sandbar renewals (DD‑008 / DD‑011) – **ASSESS**
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Disclosure Letter §8:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller asserts "ordinary course" but its own disclosure disclaims any view on that. We should not automatically treat this as Debt, but we need the facts.
- **Push back:** Request copies of the three agreements, renewal dates, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued at Completion. Commercial/finance to decide treatment after review.

### 1.14 Tax / IP warranties – **OPEN**
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; assume no resolution; keep separate from the general regime.
- **Reasoning:** This is a second attempt (with cl 13's "all Claims" sweep) to fold Tax and IP into the 20%/18‑month/tipping-basket regime by assertion. Nothing has been agreed.
- **Push back:** Mark Tax and IP as [OPEN] in our turn. Propose a separate Tax regime (seven-year period, claims from first dollar) and a separate IP regime at minimum. Do not propose unlimited liability.

### 1.15 Title evidence (DD‑012) – **MATERIAL**
- **Seller:** title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD‑012."
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD‑012 is a Seller-supplied internal document.
- **Disclosure Letter §10:** the Seller itself notes DD‑012 is "the source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Reasoning:** A company's own register is evidence of what the company recorded, not independent proof. It does not disclose encumbrances (PPSR), director/shareholder authority, or historic transfer defects.
- **Push back:** Independent ASIC extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, review of share transfer history and any shareholder/option/convertible instruments, and a Seller board minute and shareholder resolution approving the sale. Fundamental Warranties on title to remain uncapped per §1.4.

### 1.16 Office lease (DD‑007) and Mossvale (DD‑009) – **LOWER PRIORITY / CONFIRM**
- Disclosure Letter §7 and §9 characterise these as notification-only / not triggered by a share sale. These appear consistent with our understanding but we should read the clauses ourselves and require a Seller covenant to give any required notices pre-Completion. Not a negotiation point unless the documents say otherwise.

## 2. Pattern observed

Read together, the Seller's draft is constructed so that each of the following would operate cumulatively:

- whole-data-room and public-record deemed disclosure (§1.6), plus
- buyer constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers (§1.7), plus
- high tipping-to-deductible thresholds (§1.2), plus
- a reduced cap (§1.1) and reduced period (§1.3), plus
- collapse of Fundamental, Tax, IP and indemnity claims into that regime (§1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.14).

The practical result would be a warranty package under which very few claims could ever be brought, and none for the matters we are paying for. This is why the "FINAL / cleared" labelling matters: it is an attempt to lock in the architecture before the individual terms are negotiated.
